verdict.rationale: MoQ Relay's own pub/sub model connects arbitrary publishers to subscribers over native libraries (Rust, Python, Go and others). A production report shows server-side consumers (live transcription, voice ID) subscribing to live Opus audio through the relay with WebRTC-like latency. There is no evidence of a server-side agent publishing synthesized speech back into the same session, and no agent-participant integration. missing for 10: documented agent-as-participant flow, evidence of server-side speech publishing back to participants, bidirectional session semantics, independent hands-on corroboration of a realtime voice-agent loop.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, a server-side agent joins a session as a participant that receives live audio and publishes speech back in realtime

citations.quote: Browser, desktop, mobile and device clients publish Opus to one relay, which fans out to independent subscribers: an S3 archiver, Zoom Scribe Live transcription, and voice ID.
Libraries for Rust (native) and TypeScript (web), plus FFI bindings for C, Python, Kotlin, Swift, Go, and Dart.
Dynamic announcements, connecting arbitrary publishers to subscribers.
MoQ delivers WebRTC-like latency without the constraints of WebRTC.
